what: On Claude Code Stop hooks, `systemMessage` is dropped when `decision:"approve"`. It is only delivered to the agent/user when paired with `decision:"block"`. This means you cannot use `{"decision":"approve","systemMessage":"..."}` as a non-blocking way to nudge the agent at turn end — the message goes nowhere. Confirmed by the EmotionPulse plugin author in closed issue https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/43478. Implication: any Stop-hook-driven prompt requires `decision:"block"`, which is what causes the "Stop hook returned blocking error" terminal label. There is no documented workaround — the `asyncRewake` undocumented field (see memory id 111) may be the escape hatch.
why: Non-obvious platform rule. Without this memory, future sessions will waste time re-trying the `approve + systemMessage` pattern when exploring Stop hook UX. Documented by the plugin community but not in official Claude Code docs.
